_comment: Tuning thresholds, previously hard-coded as constants in dxf_reader.py. All distances are in MILLIMETRES and are applied after the drawing has been normalised to mm via $INSUNITS, so they hold regardless of the units the drawing was authored in. Edit and restart the app - no code change needed. Any key omitted here falls back to the built-in default.

floor_detection._min_floor_area_sqm_note: Lower this for villas, small offices and single-floor plans. Set to 0 to accept every closed polyline.
floor_detection._connect_tolerance_m_note: Step 2 also finds floor outlines drawn as separate lines / open polylines: ends closer than this (metres) are joined. Max 2 m was asked for; larger values start joining unrelated lines.

boundary._max_leaked_raycast_sqm_note: Ceiling on a boundary that the flood fill could not verify. When the fill leaks, the walls do not enclose the label and the four-ray box is only a guess - keeping a modest one covers a fill that escaped through a single doorway, while a large one is a label standing in open floor claiming a slab of the plate. Raise it if a large room disappears; lower it if tags in open floor are claiming rooms. At 30 it was deleting real rooms: a women's toilet measures 51.7 sq.m by rays on the typical-floor plate, and two staircases 39.5. The junk it has to stop on the other test plate runs 90 sq.m and up. Only applies where tracing is on and leaked; a traced room is capped by max_room_sqm instead.
boundary._trace_max_vs_box_ratio_note: A flood fill more than this many times larger than the four-ray box around its label, AND holding the name of a room of another family, has escaped its room through a gap; the boundary falls back to the box. Size alone is not enough now that only real walls count: a toilet with cubicle banks traces to 7-8 times the box from its label. The original case - an AHU room whose fill escaped at 9.6 times, 191 sq.m, swallowing the staircases beside it - holds staircase names and is still caught.
boundary._overlap_merge_min_size_ratio_note: Two boundaries only merge when the smaller is at least this share of the larger. Overlap is measured against the smaller of the two, so a small room standing inside a large one scores a perfect 1.0 and used to be merged with it - which is containment, not duplication. That is how an AHU room of 19.8 sq.m came out as a 167 sq.m rectangle carrying the AHU name over its neighbours. Two boundaries that really describe the same room come out close in size.
boundary._shaft_cell_note: shaft_room_to_door: the space in front of an X-marked shaft cut-out, up to the cell's door, is the shaft's room too when it is no larger than shaft_cell_max_ratio times the cut-out and shaft_cell_max_sqm.
boundary._unknown_unsized_max_sqm_note: A label whose name matches no family and states no size or area never titles a space larger than this - it is a note standing in an open floor (SERVER LOCATION over the 1000 sq.m office floor of H10 Tower 1, 9th floor).
boundary._engulf_reject_ratio_note: Reject a boundary that contains the centre of one already drawn and is at least this many times its size. Rooms do not nest, so a boundary holding another room is a fill that leaked through an opening and came back wrapping its neighbours - one boundary around an AHU room, a service lift and a hose cabinet together.
boundary._method_note: 'trace' flood-fills the real enclosed region, so angled, curved and L-shaped rooms are measured correctly. 'raycast' is the older four-ray bounding box. Tracing falls back to raycast automatically whenever a fill leaks through a gap in the walls.
boundary._seal_openings_mm_note: Gaps up to this wide in the wall linework are closed before the flood fill runs. This is only for drafting gaps where two wall lines almost meet. Door openings are closed by door swings (see doors), not by this. It used to be 900, which also sealed every WC cubicle entrance and every opening under 900 mm inside a room, so toilets were measured to the cubicle fronts instead of the wall behind them.
boundary._trace_cell_mm_note: Grid resolution for tracing. Straight walls are snapped back onto the real wall line so they stay exact; this figure only bounds the accuracy of curved runs. 25 mm roughly halves the curve error and roughly quadruples the memory.
boundary._wall_axis_ratio_note: A segment counts as axis-aligned when its long axis is at least this many times its short axis. 6.0 is about 9.5 degrees.
boundary._size_check_note: QA workbook 'Size check': every boundary with a stated size; drawn / stated outside this range is flagged.
boundary._new_rules_note: toilet_fixture_*: how far beside a toilet a WC/basin block is looked for, and the largest closed space holding one that joins the toilet. stated_size_fit_slack: a room this much larger than its label's stated size is fitted to it. open_side_*: a room with more than this share of its outline within open_side_near_mm of the plate edge, where nothing else is drawn, is not drawn.
boundary._outline_note: Every outline is cleaned after tracing, after the guardrail and in the final drawing: closed by outline_close_mm (buffer out, then in, square corners) so slits narrower than twice that fill, then opened by half outline_min_feature_mm so spikes narrower than it go. Notches and holes 100 mm and wider stay - except a sliver: a notch up to outline_sliver_max_mm wide and outline_sliver_ratio times as deep (a partition stub the outline ran in along and back out, H10 Tower 2 toilets) is filled, and a protrusion up to outline_slot_max_mm wide and outline_slot_ratio times as long (a slot up beside the next room, often the thickness of a wall the trace ran into) is cut. Not applied when it would move the area by more than outline_max_area_change.
boundary._stated_grow_note: A room traced more than stated_size_fit_slack smaller than the size its label states grows to it over a strip along one side, when that brings the side to the stated length within stated_grow_tol, the strip is not a wall hatch, not inside another room, shaft or cut-out, and a wall face runs along its far edge.
boundary._stated_claim_note: A label stating W x H may only be given to a shape whose area is within stated_size_claim_tol of W*H (0.2: 80-120%) and whose sides match W and H within stated_side_tol either way round - X claims, and the text-vs-geometry comparison (a pairing outside it is a CONFLICT, never an AGREEMENT).
boundary._leak_note: A room whose trace leaks (holds another room's name, or runs over the area cap) has the doorless openings on its leak path closed one at a time - nearest the other room's name first - re-tracing after each, at most leak_close_max times; the first trace that no longer leaks is kept and an opening it did not need stays open. Only then is every doorless opening closed. An unlabelled space a closed opening shut off (an entry lobby) joins the room. slit_max_mm: an opening narrower than this between a wall-face end and another wall line (face, cap, wall hatch edge, settled outline) is a slit, closed for every trace - doorways are 300 mm and up. hatch_edges_as_walls: the outline of each wall hatch is a wall to the tracer, so a wall drawn as a hatch with a face line missing is not a way through.
boundary._doorway_note: doorway_bridge_mm: a room whose label states its size never takes the depth of its doorway in the wall - found as the gap (up to this wide) between two pieces of one hatched wall, or between the two closing lines of a doorless opening. Only pieces no deeper than a wall, on the room's edge, and never more than 15% of the room.
boundary._face_line_note: A doorway is closed when a line on any layer lies on the wall's face line (within face_line_tol_mm, parallel) across the gap between the two wall ends, covering face_line_close_share of it, and is no longer than the gap - a door frame drawn on a shaft layer in an unnamed block (SD-3B on 181216). Gaps of face_line_gap_mm only. Never in front of a lift or a shaft (an X or a lift / shaft label within a wall's thickness across the opening), so closing a doorway never makes a lift or shaft bigger.

doors._gap_mm_note: Door-schedule gap search, and the width range for closing a wall-run gap with no door in it (only when the 'Close gaps cut in a wall run' rule is ticked).
doors._opening_keywords_note: Arcs and straight lines on a layer, or inside a block, whose name contains one of these are door or window evidence. A window closes its opening the same way a door does. An arc's centre is the hinge and its radius the leaf width; a straight door line (a leaf panel or a threshold) has a hinge at either end and its length as the width. An opening is closed only where such a hinge stands at one end of it and the width matches the gap.
doors._hinge_tol_mm_note: How far a swing's hinge may stand from the wall end at the side of the opening.
doors._bridge_mm_note: Width range of a door opening that is closed straight across. 2600 covers a double door of two 1200 mm leaves plus frames.
doors._cap_face_max_mm_note: A wall's end - a face no longer than this with a longer face leaving each of its ends on the same side - is carried across an opening only when it meets the far side within cap_corner_mm of a wall's corner (the opening between two wall ends); otherwise that ray would run through the wall's thickness into the room behind the door.

x_marks._text_gap_mm_note: How far outside an X-mark its label may stand, measured to the edge of the X rather than to its centre. A text inside the X always names it. Raise this where labels sit at the end of long leaders; lower it if labels are being pulled onto the wrong shaft. An X left with no label of its own is drawn on AI_UNKNOWN.
x_marks._enclosure_snap_margin_mm_note: An X-mark is drawn corner to corner of the shaft it marks, so the X IS the shaft. The boundary is the X's own extent, and the walls around it are used only when they hug it: every side of the wall enclosure within this many mm of the X. That is the same opening measured to the wall face. A looser enclosure belongs to the room the shaft stands in, not to the shaft - it was giving a toilet vent 11.28 sq.m in place of 3.30, and an AHU shaft 6.46 in place of 1.73.
x_marks._fallback_min_sqm_note: Smallest X-mark that still earns a boundary. Service shafts are routinely 300 mm deep - FHC-1 SHAFT is 800 x 300 - so a floor of 0.5 sq.m threw 49 real shafts away and left their labels to be sized by ray-casting instead, which is what drew them several times too large.
x_marks._void_area_threshold_sqm_note: An X-marked region larger than this is a VOID: it is drawn on AI_VOID_AREA, named VOID, and any text inside it (a landscape note, say) is taken by the void. At or below it the X marks a shaft or a cut-out.
x_marks._strip_join_note: Rule join_shaft_strips (off by default): two X-marked strips of one length face to face, up to this far apart with no wall or room between, are one shaft - both strips and the band between.
x_marks._label_claim_note: Which label an X (or any shape) may take. One standing inside it - within label_inside_tol_mm - may. One outside it (within text_radius_mm) only when it is shaft-like - its family in shaft_like_families, or its name has one of shaft_like_words - and either its stated size fits the X, or no enclosed room traced from the label is larger than the X; the nearest such label wins. A room's name (Electrical, Toilet, MEP room, Circulation, a lobby, Machine Room, Store ...) is never taken from outside. Either way the label's stated size must fit the X (boundary.stated_size_claim_tol). A refused label traces its own room as usual.
x_marks._cluster_fill_note: X marks grouped into one cluster must fill at least this share of the cluster's bounding box; two strips meeting at a corner (an L) are separate X's, never one box over the space between them.

layer_disciplines._comment: Section 6 groups layers a family keyword does not recognise by the discipline letter their name starts with, per the AIA CAD layer convention. Only a single leading letter is read - 'ST-SLAB LINE' is stairs, not structural - so add or rename entries here to match your office's convention. Anything with no single-letter prefix is grouped under 'Other layers'.

walls._comment: Which layers count as walls. Keyword match, case-insensitive, on the layer name. 'never_walls' are not walls at all - annotation, dimensions, furniture; 'exclude_from_thick' are kept out of the thick-wall tier only. Leave either list out to use the program's own defaults. This is where to send a layer that is cutting rooms in half: on the test plate the toilets are divided by the vanity counter on Q-CASE and by the sanitary fixtures on P-SANR-FIXT, both of which a flood fill treats as walls because they are continuous lines like any other.
walls._never_walls_note: M-HVAC (mechanical services: AHU fans, chilled-water pipes, pipe supports) is never a wall - its parallel pipe pairs passed the thickness test and cut H10 Tower 2's AHU rooms short. HVAC COMMENT used to be in this list. On the typical-floor test plate that layer carries the outer walls of both women's toilets, so they had no wall on one side. Add it back if your drawings use it for duct outlines.
walls._never_walls_p25_note: PLATFORM / COUNTER / KITCHEN EQUIP: kitchen platforms and counters stand inside a room and are measured as part of it (P25: AR-PLATFORM notched five kitchens and counters 0.8-1.3 sq.m each). LANDSC / PLANTING / PLANTS / VEGET: landscape linework.
walls._thickness_note: A wall is two parallel lines this far apart that run alongside each other, on any layer not in never_walls. Single lines - WC cubicle partitions, urinal screens, counter edges, centre lines - are not walls, so a room runs past them to the wall behind.
walls._panel_max_mm_note: Two lines of similar length closer than this are a panel - a door leaf, a partition board - not a wall.
walls._always_walls_note: Any line on a layer containing one of these is a wall whatever its thickness. RCC cores and shear walls are often 300-1000 mm thick, past any thickness test. UPSTAND and CUTOUT are here because pipe shafts inside AHU rooms are outlined by an upstand kerb or a slab cutout, not a wall; without them the shaft labels were absorbed into the AHU room. The diagonals of an X-mark never count, whatever their layer.
walls._facade_note: GLASS, GLAZ, CURTAIN and FACADE are walls too: the outer facade is usually curtain-wall glazing drawn as many short thin lines (A-Glass on the P285 plate, 1384 pieces), which the thickness test above would not call a wall, so rooms along the facade were not closed by it.
walls._other_level_xref_note: An XREF layer ($0$, | or XREF in its name) naming one of these levels is another level's structure laid under the plan - the basement columns under a typical floor - and is not a wall, except on basement, podium and stilt floors (rule other_level_structure).
walls._wall_hatch_note: Hatches the guardrail treats as walls (a boundary never crosses one). Regular expressions, case-insensitive, on the hatch's layer (wall_hatch_layer, wall_hatch_not_layer) and pattern name (wall_hatch_pattern). A hatch on a not_layer is never a wall; otherwise it is one when its layer or its pattern matches. One that only its pattern matches is not a wall when its layer or a block it sits in is a sign, symbol, tag, level or legend.
walls._ledge_note: A WC or basin ledge drawn 150-200 mm in front of a wall's inner face pairs with that face like a wall's other face, so toilets stopped at the ledge. A wall has two faces: a line whose nearest partner, within ledge_max_depth_mm and on one side of it only, is a face of a confirmed wall (a structure layer, or paired with a face on its far side) is a ledge and rooms trace past it to the wall. Lines on always_walls layers are never ledges. 0 turns the check off.
walls._ledge_evidence_note: Also require sanitary fixtures touching the line (within ledge_touch_mm) or at least ledge_partition_min cubicle partitions stopping at it from its room side. Spacing alone cannot tell a ledge from the outer face of the same wall (on BHUB both pair only with the wall's inner face), so leave this on.
walls._ledge_partition_note: A cubicle partition: a line across the ledge, not a wall, this long (a cubicle's depth), ending at the ledge on its room side.
walls._deadend_note: A short dead end is not a wall: a face shorter than deadend_max_len_mm with an end that touches nothing - no other wall face, cap, short line across it, wall hatch or the plate's edge within deadend_touch_mm - and any partner equally short and free at the same end. A line lying alongside it (the other side of a glass screen, a few mm off) does not close its end. On BHUB the 350 mm glass-screen ends 18 mm apart left a slit in MALE TOILET. Long walls and facade glazing are unaffected: they are long, or connected at both ends.
walls._oblique_note: A wall direction must be supported. Directions within oblique_axis_tol_deg of the floor's dominant wall direction, or square to it, always are; any other is a wall direction only when a face in it (within 1 degree) is at least oblique_min_support_mm long, or a wall hatch runs along the face. On BHUB the only 16-degree faces were the stair break symbols (897-1131 mm).
walls._breakmark_note: A zig-zag break mark is not a wall, at any angle: two pieces in line (within breakmark_collinear_deg) across a gap of at most breakmark_gap_mm, joined by a chain of short strokes (each under breakmark_stroke_ratio of the pieces, at more than breakmark_stroke_min_deg to them) stepping out to both sides of the line.

windows._note: An X-marked outline lying in a wall is a window or an opening in the wall, not a shaft (both engines, before shafts are found). It takes no room label, never becomes a room, and counts as wall when rooms are traced. Drawn on 'layer'.
windows._gap_windows_note: Windows in a wall gap (window_openings): a gap from a wall's end to the next face across its band, gap_mm long, with glazing or a louvre drawn along evidence_cover_share of it - a line on an evidence_layer_regex layer or in an evidence_block_regex block, not one matching not_evidence_regex (glass partitions, mirrors, the area-plan overlay). Across, as deep as the evidence in the gap. Part of the wall, drawn on AI_WINDOW. The X-marked windows are found as before (wall_output / x_classify).
windows._max_thickness_note: Its short side is at most this (a wall's thickness). Thicker X-marks stay shafts.
windows._face_tol_note: Each long side lies within this of a face of the wall (or the outline sits inside a wall hatch).
windows._side_share_note: At least this share of each long side must lie on a wall face. A slot that also has a wall face beyond each long side (80-400 mm out: the outer faces of two walls) is a riser between two walls and stays a shaft.
windows._wall_run_note: The wall runs on past a window: wall faces in line with each long side carry on beyond at least one of its ends for this far. A strip standing on its own (a cut-out beside a shaft) has only its own outline there and stays a shaft.
windows._hatch_note: A window may instead sit inside a wall hatch, or in a hole of one that is a slot in the wall (no wider than max_thickness_mm) - on BHUB the facade windows (W-1, 282 x 1500) sit in such a slot. Checked after the 'slot between two walls' test, so hatched walls round a real shaft do not make it a window.
windows._sides_note: What lies along each long side decides it. Wall faces running past both sides: a window in the wall. Wall faces that stop at it and carry on beyond both ends, or only its own edges with a wall running on or turning beyond one end (at least opening_min_aspect times as long as it is deep): an opening in the line of a wall. A wall face along one side and only its own edge along the other: a strip lying against a wall - a riser (BHUB's 300 mm tenant risers) - which stays a shaft.
windows._evidence_note: An X-marked outline the wall tests take for an opening in a wall is sorted by what is drawn in it. Glazing lines - lines inside it along its long side, at least glazing_min_share of it, more than glazing_edge_tol_mm from its long edges: glazing_min_lines of them (or one and a window layer word) make it a window. With none, a shaft layer word makes it a shaft strip (on to the X shafts, named from its overlay: '3.12 FP SHAFT' -> 'FP SHAFT'), else a cut-out layer word a cut-out on cutout_layer (drawn with its X, wall to the rooms, never a room, measured as a cut-out). Words are matched on the layers of its X, its outline, the lines inside and an overlay matching it within 20 mm - XREF prefix stripped, punctuation as spaces, a plural S allowed. The glazing always outranks the words; with no telling evidence the wall tests decide as before. A window whose layer says shaft or cut-out (and no window word) is listed on the QA workbook's Windows sheet.

hanging_walls._note: A wall with an object drawn under it is above floor level (a beam, a bulkhead, a drop wall): the whole element - one wall hatch, start to end - is not a wall, its area is counted in the room around it, and it is drawn on AI_HANGING_WALL (colour below) for checking. Where part of it stands on a real wall (another wall hatch, a wall layer's faces) that part stays wall. Rule 'hanging_walls' turns it off.
hanging_walls._inset_note: Objects are looked for this far inside the element's faces, so one that only touches a face (a door frame, a WC against the wall) is not under it.
hanging_walls._door_note: A door swing - an arc of a door-size radius on a door layer or in a door block - with at least door_arc_min_in_mm of it inside is an object under the wall (BHUB 1st Floor: three 600 mm cubicle doors, about 317 mm of each swing under a 300 mm structural band).
hanging_walls._fixture_note: A sanitary fixture body - the outline round one fixture block placed (WC, basin, urinal), of this size - with fixture_min_share of it inside is under the wall. A cistern partly inside a duct wall is not (the WC-ledge rule handles those).
hanging_walls._size_note: Only wall-like hatches are looked at: no thicker than this (twice the area over the perimeter) and no bigger than this; a core block with a stray arc in it stays a wall.
hanging_walls._outline_note: The lines drawn as the element's outline go with it: on a layer whose lines (each within outline_tol_mm of the outline over 80% of its length) run along own_layer_share of the outline. A real wall's face along part of it (the outer wall line beside a beam) stays.
hanging_walls._never_note: Layers and blocks never taken as objects under a wall: a lift that does not stop at a floor keeps its entrance detail in the closed wall (XA mid and high zone lifts on low-zone floors).

wall_output._note: The walls drawn in the output DXFs, on one layer, AI_WALL, built once per floor: the strips between wall face pairs (duplicates and strips absorbed by a longer one removed) and the wall hatches are one wall mass, with columns, windows and door openings cut out; the mass is split into straight runs, and runs that touch are one piece. A wall is a wall: no external / core / internal classes (drawings written before used AI_WALL_EXTERNAL / AI_WALL_CORE / AI_WALL_INTERNAL; those layers are still read as walls). Walls are never rooms and never counted in areas.
wall_output._external_note: Walls are looked for up to this distance outside the floor plate's edge; a run with half or more of it this close to the edge is joined with the other edge runs (see _groups_note).
wall_output._groups_note: Runs are joined into pieces in three groups - along the plate's edge, structure (thicker than core_min_thickness_mm, half or more on a structure_hatch_patterns hatch, or a C / L shape rejected as a column), the rest - as the three wall classes were, so a balcony's parapet stays a piece of its own and the balcony grows over it. The groups are not layers: every wall is drawn on AI_WALL, touching pieces merged into one outline.
wall_output._min_piece_note: Wall pieces smaller than this are dropped (slivers) - never one that touches another wall piece.
wall_output._simplify_note: Wall outlines are simplified to this tolerance.
wall_output._color_note: AutoCAD colour index of the AI_WALL layer (30 = orange: visible on a dark and on a white background).
wall_output._openings_note: A window or a cut-out found in a wall stays part of the wall, drawn over it on AI_WINDOW / AI_CUTOUT (the corrected walls of BHUB and XA run on through louvres and cut-outs). In the final drawing a cut-out is part of the wall only when it lies in a wall run (the wall going on past both its ends in line, or on both its long sides): one lining a wall's face inside a shaft (P285: the PHE shaft's strips, FHC-3) stays the shaft's opening. false: cut out of the wall.
wall_output._door_leaf_note: A door drawn by its leaf shut in the opening - a panel of two door-layer lines 10-80 mm apart, door_leaf_panel_mm long, framed at both ends or drawn open from one - is a door even where its swing describes no opening (P285: the shaft doors FD4 / FD8 and D4, with 325 mm swings, swings about a point outside the jamb, or a 30 degree swing in a wall drawn through the door). In a wall band it opens the band across its thickness; in a gap it opens the gap from jamb to jamb.
wall_output._lift_doors_note: A lift's entrance - a gap of lift_door_mm in the lift well's own wall, the rest of that side walled, opening onto the floor - is a door of kind lift (its doors slide; there is no swing), primary (AI_P_DOORS: between the lift and the floor in front of it). Only a lift with its stop on this floor: not LIFT PRE / PRESS, a lift lobby or machine room, or LIFT WELL BELOW (lift_not_regex).
wall_output._parapet_note: false (default): the parapet a balcony or refuge area grows over (balcony_outer_face: only along its open side, never its end walls) stays a wall on AI_WALL as well - the balcony is measured to its outer face. true: it leaves the walls of the Step 3 drawing and of the final drawing.
wall_output._door_as_line_note: Test_2: each door is drawn as a single line joining the walls either side, on the face of the room it opens into (a shaft's room run to its door, rule shaft_room_to_door_line: on the outer face, where the walls either side end). The opening it closes is kept in the door's XDATA, so the area step and the element list still read it. door_line_band_mm: a door line drawn by hand, with no opening kept, is read as a band this far either side of it. false: the opening as a closed polyline, as before.
wall_output._doors_note: Door openings - the gap in the wall a door closes - drawn on AI_DOOR: never rooms, never walls, never in an area. Found from the door swings (door_openings): an arc of door_radius_mm sweeping door_sweep_deg, on any layer (BHUB and XA draw shaft doors on the shaft's layer, part-open). At a wall: the gap from the wall's end to the next face across its band, the swing's centre within door_jamb_reach_mm of a jamb and one of its ends reaching the gap; a single leaf fits 0.55-1.35 of its radius, a pair 1.6-2.5 with a swing at each jamb. Across, the gap is as deep as the lines drawn in it along the wall (a frame: XA's shaft doors are their 76 mm frame), else the wall's thickness. With no wall gap - a WC cubicle or shaft door in a board - a full swing (75+ degrees) with its leaf drawn open gives the opening: hinge to where the leaf shuts, as deep as the board's faces (door_leaf_mm with none).
wall_output._door_between_ends_note: A door with no wall gap that shuts from one wall-line end to another (a shaft box drawn in single lines, its door block flattened with several swings) is drawn this deep across the opening.
wall_output._door_ellipses_note: A door swing drawn as an ELLIPSE (285 FD, the P285 11th floor: 139 room exits were missed) is read like an arc when it is a circle's arc - its points within door_ellipse_round of one radius from its centre (the hinge). A flattened ellipse is not a swing.
wall_output._door_kinds_note: A door is there to get out of a room. Each opening is told by the rooms on its two sides, probed door_side_probes_mm beyond its faces (the smallest room holding a point): a shaft, riser or lift on either side (door_shaft_families, or a name naming a shaft, riser, duct, vent, FHC, tenant / comm / pressurisation shaft; with no room traced, such a label within door_shaft_label_mm) is a shaft door; the same room on both sides of a door in a board (no deeper than door_cubicle_board_max_mm) is a WC cubicle door; anything else is an exit - also the same room on both sides of a door in a wall (the room was traced through its own door). This is stored on each door (XDATA). All of them are cut out of the walls. Each room's exits are listed when the areas are read (exits, exits_to).
wall_output._door_levels_note: Every door is primary or secondary (2026-10-17). Primary (AI_P_DOORS, door_color): a door between two different spaces - two rooms, or a room and the untraced common floor; a lift's and a shaft's door included. It stops a room's boundary (rule boundary_on_evidence). Secondary (AI_S_DOORS, door_secondary_color): a door inside one room - a WC cubicle's door, or a door with the same room on both sides; it never stops a room. door_main_families / door_main_area_regex / door_open_* still decide the main accessible area, which now only marks a primary door with main area on both sides (doors_primary_within_main). Drawings written before keep AI_DOOR_PRIMARY / AI_DOOR_SECONDARY, read as doors. Which way a door swings is never used.
wall_output._lift_refuse_doors_note: Rule lift_not_with_doors: a space labelled as a lift with this many hinged doors opening into it is not a lift well (a lift's doors slide); its label is refused.
wall_output._not_wall_note: A face pair with a line on one of these layers is not drawn as a wall: the area-plan overlay ('1.3 SALEABLE-...', '3.3 BALCONY'), floor finish, threshold, sill and skirting lines run alongside walls without being them.
wall_output._dedupe_note: (a) Two strips with the same four corners within this are one.
wall_output._absorb_note: (b) A strip with at least this share of its area lying on a longer strip is dropped and the longer one kept: a mirror or backsplash line (A3-GLASS, 600 mm) pairing with a wall face, and its 24-44 mm overhang past the wall.
wall_output._column_note: Columns on AI_COLUMN in the annotated (Step 3), geometry (Step 4) and final (Step 5) DXFs: the outline, a hatch (column_hatch: a pattern name, or SOLID) at column_hatch_scale, and the label column_label, in AutoCAD colour column_color.
wall_output._unhatched_note: On a floor that hatches its walls (at least hatch_share_floor of all wall-strip area on a wall hatch), a face pair with less than unhatched_strip_share of it hatched is a wall only with evidence: it continues a hatched wall in line (direction, offset and thickness within 20 mm, touching end to end), one of its faces runs at least unhatched_face_overrun_mm past it at both ends, or it lies on the floor plate's edge band. Otherwise it is dropped from the walls and the tracer ('unhatched pair inside a room'). A strip a room grows over to reach its stated size is never a wall either ('room-size veto').

_geometry_sequence_note: The order the geometry engine (Step 4) works in. Each stage skips a shape an earlier stage took, so the order decides who gets a shape two could claim. Stages: columns (the column shapes, as obstacles: a shape inside one is no room), x_marks (every X mark, as evidence only - its place is no room, a lift-size X is a lift well for the lobby test, a long X with treads both sides a staircase's well), staircases, toilets, lift_wells (lift-size squares in a bank, as evidence for the lobby test), lift_lobbies (a space with lift wells along both longer sides - a machine room when none of those lifts has a door onto it), service_lobbies (the space a staircase's door opens into), rooms. The engine never reports a shaft, lift, window, cut-out, column or void: those are Step 3's (the X sequence, xplace.py). A stage left out still runs, after the listed ones; an older list's shafts is x_marks, its windows is gone.

geometry_engine._note: Settings of the geometry engine (Step 4) that are not drawing measurements (those are in geo_profiles.json).
geometry_engine._stair_guard_inset_note: The guardrail cuts a boundary where it crosses a wall. For a staircase, lines lying more than this far inside its outline - treads, flights, handrails - do not count as walls; only walls on its outline or crossing in from outside do.
geometry_engine._stair_guard_min_keep_note: If a guardrail cut would leave less than this share of a staircase's area, the cut is skipped and the staircase kept whole (evidence: 'guardrail cut skipped').
geometry_engine._column_in_wall_note: A piece no thicker than column_in_wall_max_mm lying in a wall line - wall-layer faces along both its long sides over column_in_wall_face_share of each - is that wall, never a column (the 755 x 200 jambs of the P285 lift openings were cut out of the walls as columns).
geometry_engine._column_hollow_note: A column is solid: a candidate whose outline (convex hull) area is more than this many times its filled area is a C / L shaped core wall, not a column (on BHUB 1st Floor two 3150 x 3450 C-shapes on the column layer). Those go to the walls (AI_WALL).

curves._sagitta_tolerance_mm_note: Maximum chord deviation when flattening arcs and polyline bulges into line segments. Smaller is more accurate and slower.

annotation._block_recursion_depth_note: How many INSERT levels to descend when collecting text and geometry. Was fixed at 1; production drawings routinely nest three or four deep.
annotation._hatch_note: Fill every drawn boundary with a solid hatch in its family colour, on the same layer as the outline. The hatch is associative (it follows the outline when the boundary is edited in CAD), leaves voids open, and is sent to the back so walls and texts stay readable. hatch_transparency runs 0 (solid) to 0.9. Set hatch to false for outlines only. Step 4 reads only the outlines, never the hatch.

label_filters._comment: Which texts can name a room. 'ignore_patterns' are never room names at all (dimensions, levels, UP/DN). 'device_tag_patterns' are equipment tags - they can still label a boundary if nothing better is inside it, but they lose to any text that matches a family keyword. This is what stopped the tag INID04 outranking the room name PRESS. Patterns are case-insensitive regexes matched against the whole text.
label_filters._max_room_name_chars_note: Longer than this and the text is a drawing note, not a room name - judged before the family keywords, because a sentence like 'FOR DETAILS OF STAIRCASE-01 REFER DRG' contains STAIRCASE and was being ranked as a room. Raise it if a project genuinely uses long room names.
label_filters._equipment_tags_note: Devices drawn on the plan that are also family keywords, so every other test reads them as room names and gives them a boundary of their own - a fire hose reel on a toilet wall was taking half the toilet. Matched as whole strings, so 'FHC' is a cabinet while 'FHC ROOM' is still a room. They can still title an X-marked shaft that holds nothing better.
label_filters._fixture_layers_note: Text on a layer whose name contains one of these is a label on a sanitary fixture or fitting (TB, EWC, WB, HF, TPH...) and is never a room name, whatever it says. On A-109 the second tower's fixture blocks carry about 150 such labels and the first tower's carry none: read as room names they took the toilets apart into TB and EWC boxes and left the toilet's own name without a room. Matched anywhere in the layer name, case-insensitive.

quantities._core_families_note: Used for the core-efficiency KPI and deducted from the net deck-sheet area.
quantities._studs_per_sqm_note: Given in the module brief as a fixed rate, so it is a constant rather than a user input.
quantities._overlap_flag_ratio_note: Room pairs overlapping by at least this much, but below overlap_merge_ratio, are reported as suspect rather than merged.

linear_quantities._comment: Layer-name keyword rules for grouping polyline run lengths by discipline. Same shape as family_rules.json: case-insensitive substring match, first hit wins.

block_inventory._comment: Keyword rules for classifying INSERT block names into countable categories. Produces the raw inventory for fixture, sprinkler and door/window counting.

area_statement._note: Area Statement. Every room is filed under one canonical category (area_statement.CATEGORIES); X-marked slab openings are deducted, walled shaft rooms are listed but not deducted. sale area = plinth / sale_area_factor; sq.ft = sq.m x sqft_per_sqm. 'templates' compose a client's columns from the canonical categories: each column = one category or the sum of several; categories no column names get a column of their own. 'template' picks the one used by default.

285._note: 285 FD Tower 1 sheet: AHU column holds the AHU rooms and the AHU shafts; one pressure-shaft column for staircase and lobby pressurisation.

bhub._note: BHUB sheet: lobby pressurisation under LIFT LOBBY PREZ SHAFT.

refuge_off_plinth._note: H10 Tower 3 sheet: refuge areas are taken off the plinth as well as stairs and lifts.

area_statement._min_unnamed_note: An unnamed X-marked opening smaller than this (sq.m) is a pipe sleeve, not a shaft: listed, not deducted. Named shafts are deducted whatever their size.
area_statement._gross_to_facade_note: A floor outline on a slab-projection layer (facade.slab_layer_words) runs to the slab edge; with this on, gross is measured to the outer face of the facade instead (facade.py), as a take-off 'inc glass' is.

geometry_types._comment: Rooms the text cannot name are named from what is drawn in them: a staircase from its evenly spaced treads, a toilet from its sanitary fixtures.
geometry_types._stair_part_note: Rule stairs_by_treads: a flight with no room of its own is traced from its middle (its treads not walls to that trace, whatever layer draws them, nor to the wall guardrail). It is a staircase of 8 sq.m or more, or of stair_part_min_sqm or more when a staircase is traced within stair_part_reach_mm of it - the other part of that staircase (the flight down to the basement behind a wall across the ground-floor stair core, H10 Tower 1), named as it.

facade._note: Gross to the outer face of the facade when the floor outline is the slab edge: the slab is rasterised (cell_mm) with every line on a facade layer as a barrier, gaps up to gap_close_mm closed, and filled from outside; what the fill reaches inside the slab is outside the facade. The barrier band along it counts band_share in. A fill reaching more than max_outside_share of the slab leaked into the building: no answer, the slab stays the gross.

glass._note: Glass partitions and glazing (elements.py): a line on a glass / glazing / curtain-wall layer or in a glass block, not a mirror, not in a window or a door. Neighbouring lines pair_mm apart are one strip; a single line is a single_line_width_mm band. Drawn on AI_GLASS (colour below): never a wall, never a room, never in an area.

wall_trace._note: What is wall (walltrace.py): two faces a wall's thickness apart on a wall layer, paired nearest-first, confirmed by the hatch found inside them (every piece of a hatch, not only its largest loop). Decides the walls on AI_WALL and the wall area / length in the Step 3 drawing and the final drawing alike; room tracing is not affected. Rule 'wall_trace' turns it off.
wall_trace._structure_note: Structure drawn on a structure layer (the last part of the name matching structure_layer_regex and not a wall layer - BHUB's 400-450 mm concrete core walls on XREF-T1_STR$1$COLUMN) is paired like a wall, up to structure_thickness_max_mm apart, and kept only where the structure hatch fills it and it runs at least structure_min_run_mm and twice its thickness: a column stays a column.
wall_trace._plate_edge_note: An unhatched strip with one face on the floor plate's edge (plate_edge_share of it within plate_edge_tol_mm) and a wall strip on its other face is the slab edge outside that wall, not wall (the 200 mm x 39.5 m band along the XA tower's facade).
wall_trace._arc_note: Curved walls: arcs on wall layers (ARCs and bulged polyline spans) with centres within arc_centre_tol_mm are concentric; arcs within arc_same_face_mm of the same radius are one face; each face pairs with the nearest face outside it thickness_min_mm - thickness_max_mm away.
wall_trace._hatch_fill_note: The hatch is the wall where its faces do not pair: a piece of wall hatch left over beside a traced wall, no wider than block_min_side_mm, of at least hatch_fill_min_sqm, is wall (P-14 6th floor: the 500 x 300 feet of the L-shaped concrete columns, whose faces are 500 mm apart; a block wall carried on behind a basin niche that breaks its face). Wider pieces stay shafts, columns or review blocks. Where filled pieces cover hatch_bridge_share of a gap of up to hatch_bridge_max_mm between two strips of one band, the band is carried across the gap (the wall keeps its face behind the niche). Door openings are cut out.
wall_trace._hatch_fill_thickness_note: No wider than a wall is the piece's thickness, not its box: eroded by half of hatch_fill_max_thickness_mm nothing is left, or only specks of up to hatch_fill_core_sqm along a piece at least three times that long (a thick wall's corner; a 500 x 600 column is short and stays a column). Such a piece is wall beside a traced wall, or anywhere when lines drawn on any layer run along hatch_fill_edged_share of its outline (the P285 toilet walls: 12 m x 1.3 m by their box, 200 mm thick, faces on HVAC COMMENTS).
wall_trace._solid_not_shaft_note: Solid fill is concrete, never a shaft: a solid-filled piece left over beside a shaft label is wall where it stands against a traced wall or is edged (the six 5.4 sq.m corner blocks by the P285 shafts). With solid_against_wall_is_wall, any solid piece left over against a traced wall is wall, label or not (the RCC blocks at P285's wall ends; the final drawing reads no labels, so this makes it draw them as Step 3 does). Else a column or review.
wall_trace._unfilled_sandwich_note: An unhatched strip closed at both ends between two unhatched walls (XA tower 200 | 151 | 200): 'gap' = not wall, 'wall' = counted.

confidence._note: Room confidence (confidence.py): starts at 'base' and moves with the evidence - stated size / area matched or missed, traced or only a box, X-marked, family, tag names, other labels inside, grown, leak cut. High at 'high' or above, Medium at 'medium' or above, Low below. 'weights' overrides any of the steps.

slab_edge_lines._comment: A long single line on a detail or section layer that runs through X-marked shafts is the edge of the slab, not a wall (rule slab_edge_not_boundary; P285: the 13.8 m line on a-details by the east balcony). It bounds no room and no wall, in Step 3 and in the geometry engine.
slab_edge_lines._through_note: How far the line must run inside an X-marked box (50 mm in from its sides) to be the slab edge.

rooms_and_doors._comment: What a floor's rooms and doors settle together (Test_2; the stair's open well - an X the X sequence made a void between two flights - and rules shaft_room_mep, shaft_room_to_door_line, lift_no_door_machine_room, wall_gaps_filled).
rooms_and_doors._shaft_room_note: A room of one of shaft_room_families sharing shaft_room_side_mm or more of its outline with an X-marked shaft, and with a door (door_touch_mm of the door along its outline, or half the door's width), is the shaft's room: drawn in shaft_room_family (AI_MEP) - when it is no larger than shaft_room_max_sqm and is named for a shaft (TEN, ELE SHAFT, FHC ...), for the X beside it, or not at all. A refuge area or a store beside a shaft is not.
rooms_and_doors._lift_note: A lift with no door whose side faces a lift machine room across no more than this (a wall) is drawn in the Machine Room family.
rooms_and_doors._wall_gap_note: The wall left between the rooms: a wall-hatched piece, or a strip no wider than wall_gap_thin_mm enclosed by rooms, doors and walls with no label in it (not a column's casing, not the rest of a door's opening), between wall_gap_min_sqm and wall_gap_max_sqm, goes on AI_WALL.

element_engine._comment: The element identification engine (elementid.py): every door, staircase, lift lobby, service lobby and lift machine room classified again from the evidence drawn round it with a 0-100 confidence score; every shaft, lift, window, cut-out, column and void recorded as Step 3 decided it (the X sequence, xplace.py), never scored again. It changes no area and no class.
element_engine._bands_note: auto_min and up: auto-classified (high_min and up High, else Medium); review_min to auto_min: Low, 'possible <class>', needs review; under review_min: Unresolved, held.
element_engine._tie_margin_note: Two classes within this many points are settled by the tie-break rules; both under auto_min leave the element Unresolved.
element_engine._review_note: Elements marked on the review layer: Low and Unresolved ones, and - review_disputed - those the engine classifies otherwise than they are drawn. The review layer is never a room and its notes are never labels.
element_engine._door_layer_treads_note: Treads are read from the door layer only when none are found without it (some drawings draw the stair on the door layer), and only in a run of at least this many evenly spaced parallel lines - a door's leaf is never a tread.

x_placement._note: The X sequence (xplace.py, 2026-10-16, final): every X mark, on any layer and of any size, is a void to start with, then decided once - 2 shaft, 3 lift, 4 window, 5 cut-out, 6 column, 7 void - and nothing overrides it (not the Step 3 family, the Geometry tab, the element or geometry engine, the final drawing). wall_gap_mm: a shaft's X has a wall within this of a side (on BHUB, Centaurus, P285 and XA every real shaft is within 20 mm, the nearest X that is not a shaft 75 mm). run_*: the wall carries on past an end of the X at its thickness (within run_tol_mm), over run_probe_mm, covering run_cover of it - the X is an opening in the wall. tag_reach_mm: a door / window / cut-out tag this close to an X describes it. *_tag_re: the tag patterns; a shaft's name is never a tag, and a code with no digit and two vowels is a word.
x_placement._in_room_note: Step 5 never makes an X standing in a room a cut-out: inside the room's outline, or in a notch the room was traced round (within in_room_reach_mm of it, inside its convex hull and no other room's).
x_placement._in_space_note: The element pipeline (rule element_pipeline, 2026-10-17) decides every X before any room is traced from a label. An X stands in a room when the space traced from a point in_space_probe_mm outside one of its sides closes - between in_space_min_sqm and in_space_max_sqm, and no more than in_space_plate_share of the plate (the plate's edge closes every trace; the open floor is no room) - and holds the X (inside its outline, or in a notch within in_room_reach_mm and inside its convex hull). A stair's well has a flight on either side within well_reach_mm.
x_placement._slot_note: A slot - an X narrower than slot_side_mm, or smaller than slot_area_sqm - that the wall mass holds for slot_in_wall_share of it is inside the wall (steps 4 and 5): a sleeve slot, never a shaft.
x_placement._lift_note: Step 3, the lift rules: an X with a LIFT label, or of lift size (both sides within lift_side_mm, the long side at most lift_aspect_max times the short) and not named for a shaft, walled (a wall within wall_gap_mm) on at least lift_walled_sides sides. Step 2 leaves exactly those X marks to it.

spaces._note: Rule rooms_from_spaces (2026-10-17): the rooms are the enclosed spaces of the floor, found with no text and named last. The free floor is cut into its connected pieces on a grid of grid_mm cells (every wall line, door closure and decided outline sealed by one cell); a piece of open_floor_sqm or more - or holding open_floor_share of the free floor (a small plate's open floor is under 1000 sq.m) - is the open floor (no room), one narrower than 2 x min_half_width_mm is a wall cavity or a doorway strip, one under min_sqm is nothing; every other piece is traced once at its widest point. A space with no text and no door under pocket_max_sqm, or under edge_pocket_max_sqm along the plate's edge, is a pocket, not a room. Two lift banks facing each other lobby_gap_mm apart hold a lobby closed at their ends (lobby_min_sqm or more). An unnamed space is drawn (draw_unnamed) as unnamed_label on the Unknown family's layer. The shaft room's size is rooms_and_doors.shaft_room_max_sqm.
